correctness.rationale: For a pair at distance 2h write s=sqrt(1−h^2), and u,w for the midpoint and difference components of a perturbation of norm t. The fourth-power difference in absolute value is 8h|w|(1+t^2+2su). For 0<h<1 a maximizer has |w|>0; reflecting a negative u strictly increases the product, and transferring any perpendicular component to |w| at fixed u,t strictly increases it. The resulting expression is strictly increasing in t for every nonzero angular objective, so t=a. Its angular derivative has sign Q−Pc−2Qc^2; this strictly decreases from positive to negative for Q>0 and yields exactly one tilt, with the two orientations given by the sign of w. At the optimum, differentiating h times the angular objective and using Pc=2as(1−2c^2) gives a positive factor sqrt(1−c^2) times [P+(4a^2/P)(1−2c^2)(2s^2−1)], strictly positive since P^2>=4a^2 and the product has absolute value <1 in the open interval. Thus the minimizing pairs are exactly those at distance d, with the endpoint separated by continuity and direct antipodal computation. The ratio Q/P is invariant under reciprocal radius and is uniquely largest at a=1; c strictly increases with this ratio. This establishes quartic reciprocity, the strict improvement over the c=0 benchmark, and the endpoint value. All computations are analytic and require only a real two-plane; the realification of a complex space is valid.
